title: Elastic chunking and pressure-signaling to mitigate burst backpressure at extreme QPS
creator: Leah Moreno
description:
Background: Production clusters have exhibited tail latency spikes and intermittent OOMs when sustained QPS exceeds 6k req/s per GPU under mixed sequence-length workloads. Existing microbatch admission only uses fixed thresholds (num_requests and aggregate_tokens) which are brittle under bursty arrival patterns and skewed KV hotkeys. This ticket proposes a combined "elastic chunking" and pressure-signaling architecture to smooth admission, preserve KV cache hotness, and maintain p95 latency SLOs while avoiding GPU memory overcommit.

Goals: 1) Prevent large instantaneous microbatches from causing KV cache reclaim storms or kernel memory pressure. 2) Keep short-sequence requests fast via a fast-path that avoids full batching when safe. 3) Signal upstream routers to shed or reroute work before GPU memory crosses critical thresholds. 4) Provide observable metrics and feature flags for controlled rollouts.

Proposal summary:
- Elastic chunking: split admitted requests into smaller execution chunks at runtime based on a token-headroom estimate. Instead of waiting to fill a microbatch to target N requests, the admission controller allows a capped "chunk_size" (in tokens) determined by available GPU headroom and expected KV memory retention. Large requests are executed as multiple chunks with KV cache pointers preserved between chunks to minimize recomputation.
- Pressure-signaling state machine: GPUs export a 4-state pressure signal (GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED). States computed from a weighted combination of: GPU memory usage %, KV cache occupancy delta (hotset churn), current active KV slabs, and queue depth growth rate. Transitions include hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.
- Token-aware soft admission: admission now considers per-request token cost and current token_headroom_budget. Requests are admitted only if their token cost plus current inflight_token_count <= token_headroom_budget * soft_factor. Soft_factor decays when the state moves toward ORANGE/RED.
- KV hotset reservation: reserve a small portion of GPU memory for the top-N KV entries (by hotness), protected from eviction while pressure is GREEN/YELLOW. When moving to ORANGE/RED, fallbacks start evicting cold slabs and trigger an upstream reduction in admitted long sequences (via pressure signal).
- Fast-path bypass: short requests (< 32 tokens or cached prefix hit) can take a low-latency fast-path if current state is GREEN or YELLOW and observed kernel queue is empty. This preserves p50/p90 for short interactions.

Implementation plan: phase A (core runtime + metrics), phase B (router integration + rollout flags), phase C (observability, canary).
Phase A tasks:
- admission: add token_headroom estimator and chunking scheduler (ENG change in runtime admission module).
- execution: support multi-chunk execution with KV pointer persistence per request. Add checkpointing of partial KV usage metadata into in-memory per-request context.
- pressure-signal exporter: new endpoint /metrics/gpu_pressure exposing state and inputs.
- default policies: define thresholds used for GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED with sensible defaults for rtx6000-like GPUs.

Phase B tasks:
- router: honor pressure signal (prefer local GPU when GREEN, route to less-loaded region when ORANGE, apply rate-limited shedding when RED).
- autoscaler: integrate pressure metrics to trigger burst capacity spin-up before OOM.

Observability & experiments:
- New dashboard showing p95 latency, inflight_token_count, token_headroom_budget, KV_hotset_size, KV_eviction_rate, GPU_pressure_state.
- Experiment matrix: synthetic burst tests at 2x/3x baseline QPS, mixed seq length distributions (short/medium/long), and real production replay traffic. Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory percentage, KV slab eviction rate, fraction of requests chunked, and failure rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Under 3x baseline sustained QPS with production-like seq distribution, p95 improves by >= 25% relative to current microbatching baseline, and no OOMs observed in 30-minute runs.
- Fast-path p50 remains within 5% of baseline.
- Pressure transitions and router reaction observed in canary rollout.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Multi-chunk execution increases kernel launch frequency and may raise throughput overhead; mitigations include batching chunk boundaries across requests and small warm-up kernels.
- KV pointer persistence consumes additional per-request metadata memory; we will cap number of concurrent multi-chunk requests and account for it in token_headroom_budget.
- Incorrect threshold tuning may cause premature shedding; we will start conservative and iterate with canary loads.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.internal/redwood/elastic-chunking-pressure-signaling
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4057 (WIP)
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/pressure/elastic-chunking

Next steps / TODOs:
- Arjun: land admission estimator prototype behind feature flag (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Leah: prepare synthetic workload harness and base test plan (ETA 2026-03-12, done).
- SRE: add e2e alert that triggers when GPU_pressure_state == RED for > 15s (coord with infra).

Notes on tuning knobs: token_headroom_budget should be percentile-aware (e.g., 95th of observed per-minute per-GPU memory footprint) and include margin for concurrent evictions. Soft_factor default = 0.8 in GREEN, 0.6 in YELLOW, decays to 0.4 in ORANGE. Hysteresis windows: 10s enter/30s exit for ORANGE/RED to avoid oscillation.
